scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You tap your card, and two seconds later, approved. But in those two seconds, your payment went on a trip.

scenes.name: tap
scenes.text: The card's chip talks to the machine by NFC, and creates a one time code for this payment, so copying it is useless.

scenes.name: acq
scenes.text: The machine sends the amount and card details to the shop's bank, called the acquirer.

scenes.name: net
scenes.text: The acquirer passes it to the card network, like Visa, Mastercard or RuPay, which routes it to the bank that issued your card.

scenes.name: check
scenes.text: Your bank checks your limit, looks for fraud patterns, and verifies the PIN if needed. Then it says approve, or decline.

scenes.name: back
scenes.text: That answer travels back the same path, and the machine beeps. All in a second or two.

scenes.name: settle
scenes.text: The money actually moves later, usually by the next day, when banks settle up in batches.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Tap, network, bank, beep. A round trip in seconds. Follow for more on how things really work.
